# `==` between structs holding a list, an option or another struct compares
# them field by field on every target, as the interpreter does, and so does
# `==` between two lists and between two options.
#
# Go wrote each as its own ==: a struct holding a slice, and a slice, did not
# compile (`struct containing []string cannot be compared`), and an option is
# a pointer, so two options holding 1 were unequal, and so were two structs
# holding them. JavaScript's === is an array's identity, so two lists written
# alike were unequal there. Both now write the comparison out from the type,
# as html already did for a struct (Go's goEqualer, JavaScript's jsEqual).

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout 'ok +4 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

struct Pair {
    left  int
    right int
}

struct Tagged {
    name string
    tags list[string]
}

struct Box {
    inner Tagged
    maybe option[int]
    pairs list[Pair]
}

component page ui.node {
    var name = "a"
    var tag = "x"
    var n = 1

    ui.text(value=name)
}

func tagged(name string, tag string) Tagged {
    return {name=name, tags=[tag]}
}

func box(name string, tag string, n int) Box {
    return {inner=tagged(name, tag), maybe=n, pairs=[{left=n, right=n}]}
}

func testAStructHoldingAListComparesItsElements(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(tagged(c.name, c.tag) == tagged(c.name, c.tag))
    t.assert(tagged(c.name, c.tag) != tagged(c.name, "y"))
    t.assert(tagged(c.name, c.tag) != Tagged{name=c.name, tags=[]})
}

func testListsCompareElementByElement(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert([c.name, c.tag] == [c.name, c.tag])
    t.assert([c.name] != [c.name, c.tag])
    t.assert([tagged(c.name, c.tag)] == [tagged(c.name, c.tag)])
}

func testAStructHoldingAnOptionComparesWhatItHolds(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.assert(box(c.name, c.tag, c.n) == box(c.name, c.tag, c.n))
    t.assert(box(c.name, c.tag, c.n) != box(c.name, c.tag, c.n + 1))
    t.assert(box(c.name, c.tag, c.n) != Box{inner=tagged(c.name, c.tag), pairs=[{left=c.n, right=c.n}]})
}

func testAnOptionOfAStructComparesWhatItHolds(t test.Test, c page) {
    var some option[Tagged] = tagged(c.name, c.tag)
    var none option[Tagged] = null
    t.assert(some == tagged(c.name, c.tag))
    t.assert(some != none)
    t.assert(none == null)
    var x option[int] = c.n
    var y option[int] = c.n
    t.assert(x == y)
}
